title: Build a RAG Pipeline from Scratch

sections.subtitle: The pipeline
sections.description:
RAG connects a retriever to a generator. The retriever finds relevant chunks; the generator answers using those chunks as context.

The quality of the answer is capped by the quality of retrieval. Start there.

sections.subtitle: Chunking and embeddings
sections.description:
Chunks should be small enough to be specific and large enough to be meaningful. Overlap preserves context across boundaries.

An embedding maps a chunk to a vector. Similar meaning should produce nearby vectors.

consoleBlock.py:
text = """Retrieval augmented generation combines a retriever with a generator.
Chunking decides what the retriever can find.
Embeddings turn chunks into vectors."""

chunks = [chunk.strip() for chunk in text.split(".") if chunk.strip()]

for index, chunk in enumerate(chunks, start=1):
    print(index, chunk)

sections.subtitle: Rank with cosine similarity
sections.description:
Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors. It ignores magnitude, which is useful when embedding lengths vary.

In production, a vector database handles this search at scale.
